subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an academic who analyzed a treatise on poison tied to celestial mechanics and realized the trigger is location-based, not temporal. He passed a key to Daz after recognizing the keep’s security is compromised by scholarly distraction.
source_quote: I had the treatise open in front of me. *On the Punctual Tears.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a pragmatic investigator who received a key from Grygum and is now entangled in the murder mystery. He understands the academic distraction has left the keep vulnerable and is aware of Daral’s precarious position.
source_quote: Totally, totally," Zalthir said, in a voice that recorded everything.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a paranoid but perceptive figure who believes he’s being framed for murder. He possesses the poison book, suspects Daz and Thorin are his only protectors, and fears Zalthir will learn of his drunken, incriminating remarks about dragonborn.
source_quote: He had the poison book. He'd worked out someone wanted him to take the fall.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a meticulous scholar whose voice records everything and whose analytical nature makes him a threat to anyone with hidden truths. He is unaware of Daral’s drunken comments but is being referenced as a looming consequence.
source_quote: Totally, totally," Zalthir said, in a voice that recorded everything.

subject: Brother Vareth
fact: Brother Vareth has appropriated Grygum’s incomplete answer to the Question of the Age and turned it into a published thesis, sparking mass academic frenzy and diverting attention from the ongoing murder investigation.
source_quote: He'd taken my answer to the Question of the Age... and he'd turned it into a thing. A fourth corner.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was a paranoid scholar who carried a key tied to a stolen sapphire with a summoning enchantment. He removed the key from his possession because he understood that only a corpse cannot be bound by its magic.
source_quote: So if you wanted a man's key, the cleanest way to free it from his possession was to make him a corpse.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is blunt and unadorned in truth-telling. He told Daral that solving the murder grants access to any book in Candlekeep — but emphasized the reward is worthless, undercutting any false hope.
source_quote: Look, I'm just saying, if we solve the murder, we get any book in the place." A beat. "We get shit.

subject: Avowed Community
fact: The Avowed Community has abandoned all urgent duties — including the murder of a scholar and the threat of a poisoned book — to obsess over a newly published academic thesis, revealing their institutional prioritization of scholarship over survival.
source_quote: The whole Avowed community wanted, right then and there, to drop everything and debate it in the Grand Hall.

subject: Followers of Kelemvor
fact: The Followers of Kelemvor have established through their god’s cryptic doctrine that a dead person possesses nothing, while the undead retain possession — a principle critical to understanding the summoning enchantment on the stolen sapphire.
source_quote: An undead can. A dead man can't. The followers of Kelemvor have made that point very clear...

subject: murder of the scholar
fact: A scholar has been murdered, likely via a poison tied to celestial mechanics, and the crime scene involves a stolen sapphire with a summoning enchantment that requires the victim to be dead to free a possessed object.
source_quote: There is a poisoned book and a dead scholar.

subject: publication of the fourth corner
fact: Brother Vareth published a revision of Grygum’s incomplete answer to the Question of the Age, triggering a mass academic frenzy that diverted all attention from the murder investigation and left the keep unguarded.
source_quote: He'd turned it into a thing. A fourth corner. And he had told everyone.

subject: the poison book
fact: The poison book is a dangerous artifact tied to celestial mechanics and the timing of midnight. It is currently in Daral’s possession, and he believes it was planted to frame him for the scholar’s murder.
source_quote: He had the poison book. He'd worked out someone wanted him to take the fall.

subject: the stolen sapphire
fact: The stolen sapphire carries a summoning enchantment that can only pull items from corpses — not the living or undead. This mechanism explains why Kalan Strongbranch removed his key and why the scholar was killed.
source_quote: The stolen sapphire carried a summoning working — it could pull an item to you, but only an item not in anyone's possession.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch's key
fact: Kalan Strongbranch's key once hung around his neck and was later passed to Daz. It is now in a state of transit, no longer possessed by its original owner, and potentially subject to the sapphire’s summoning magic.
source_quote: I had a key on me. It had hung around Kalan Strongbranch's neck once.

subject: Zalthir's knowledge of dragonborn remarks
fact: Daral made drunken, incriminating remarks about dragonborn in a barroom setting, and fears Zalthir will learn of them. Zalthir’s recorded voice makes this an unresolved threat that could destroy Daral’s credibility or safety.
source_quote: He was very much hoping nobody would mention to Zalthir what he'd said about dragonborn. Drunk, barroom talk, not meant to be taken seriously.

subject: the identity of the poisoner
fact: The poisoner used the sapphire’s summoning enchantment to kill the scholar by making him a corpse, thereby freeing the key. The killer’s identity remains unknown, but the act reveals deep knowledge of Kelemvor’s doctrine and celestial mechanics.
source_quote: So if you wanted a man's key, the cleanest way to free it from his possession was to make him a corpse.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is an academic fortress now dangerously unguarded. The entire Avowed Community has abandoned security to debate a new thesis, leaving dining halls, chambers, and corridors vulnerable to further murders or theft.
source_quote: The keep was suddenly full of rooms nobody would be watching. The dining room, for one.

subject: time of midnight
fact: Midnight is not a clock-based event in this context, but a celestial alignment — the moment the sun is directly opposite on the globe. The poison’s trigger is location-based, making the passage of time irrelevant unless one moves to avoid the dark side of the world.
source_quote: Midnight is when the sun is directly on the other side of the globe from you.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the investigator who filed Daral under 'desperate' and later took custody of the key to perform a divining spell, noting its cleanliness and the implications for the summoning magic's true target.
source_quote: I took custody of the key, set my fingers to the cold iron of it, and let the spell read the object the way an auditor reads an account someone else kept.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the strategist who fixated on the timeline of the book and the possibility that Daral is the killer, repeatedly pressing the logical implication that tampering occurred before or after the book was handed over.
source_quote: So what I'm saying is that the timeline of the book seems to be a very important thing at this point.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is the accused man who provided the location of the Oak Tree Apothecary and the details of when and how the book was left under the tree, but insisted he never handed it to anyone — his testimony became central to the timeline investigation.
source_quote: He'd dropped the book under the evergreen tree, next to the other gifts, around 11am on Deadwinter's Eve... he hadn't handed it to anybody. The book got picked up by Janussi at dinner.

subject: Leuwin
fact: Leuwin is the elderly, absent-minded satyr druid at the Oak Tree Apothecary, who is expected to identify the poison from the book definitively, though he has not yet been encountered.
source_quote: A satyr druid named Leuwin, elderly and absent-minded, with a pet squirrel, who could identify the poison from the book definitively.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the investigator who requested the key be checked for ongoing magic, prompting Daz to perform the divining spell that revealed the key was clean and unrelated to the summoning spell.
source_quote: Zalthir wanted it checked for ongoing magic, and that is my function, not his. 'I can read it,' I said.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is the avowed minder assigned to prevent the four strangers from accessing the library's contents, who left his post to attend Grygum's theological debate, inadvertently granting the investigators an hour of unsupervised time.
source_quote: Fembris asked to leave. Our minder, the avowed assigned to ensure four armed strangers didn't help themselves to the contents of the world's most dangerous library, wanted to attend a debate.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the orc theologian whose new theology is the subject of a major debate in the Oval Theater, drawing half the avowed and forcing Bookwyrm to attend despite political risk.
source_quote: Grygum's debate, as it turned out — a disputation in the Oval Theater on his new theology, with half the avowed already in attendance and Bookwyrm herself unable to politically afford to miss it.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is a high authority in the library who could not politically afford to miss Grygum’s debate, indicating her influence and the political weight of the theological conflict.
source_quote: Bookwyrm herself unable to politically afford to miss it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is the oozing entity who attempted to assist Daz in resolving the hidden connection between the gem, the key, and the murdered man, but failed, sinking back into himself in disappointment.
source_quote: Glabbagool tried to help, an eye surfacing through the ooze, hopeful, and I came up emptier still, and the eye sank back down, dolefully, into the rest of him.

subject: the Avowed
fact: The Avowed are the organized guardians of the library, tasked with preventing unauthorized access by strangers, and are sufficiently numerous and politically engaged to have members attending Grygum’s debate.
source_quote: the avowed assigned to ensure four armed strangers didn't help themselves to the contents of the world's most dangerous library... half the avowed already in attendance.

subject: the divining of the key
fact: Daz performed a divining spell on the key, confirming it was clean — not bound to the summoning spell, not created by it, and carrying no enchantment — which shifted the investigation to the sapphire gem as the true anchor of the magic.
source_quote: The key was clean. Not linked to that spell, not created by it, carrying no quiet enchantment under the surface.

subject: the theft of the original key
fact: The original key used in the summoning spell was stolen, forcing the perpetrator to cast a duplicate into the sapphire gem as a backup — a move that reveals the killer anticipated being tracked.
source_quote: The summoning had been worked on a *different* key.

subject: the Oak Tree Apothecary
fact: The Oak Tree Apothecary is a treehouse grown into the roots of an evergreen oak, located between the Sea Warden's Tower and the House of Mechanus, where Leuwin is expected to identify the poison.
source_quote: The Oak Tree Apothecary, he said, between the Sea Warden's Tower and the House of Mechanus, a treehouse grown into the roots of an evergreen oak.

subject: the Oval Theater
fact: The Oval Theater is the venue for Grygum’s theological debate, a site of high political and religious significance where Bookwyrm and half the Avowed were compelled to attend.
source_quote: a disputation in the Oval Theater on his new theology, with half the avowed already in attendance and Bookwyrm herself unable to politically afford to miss it.

subject: the sapphire gem
fact: The sapphire gem is not mere decoration — it is the retrieval token for the summoning spell, functioning as a backup against theft of the original key, and must be the same gem used to both store and recall the object.
source_quote: The sapphire isn't decoration: it's the retrieval token, and it has to be the *same* sapphire both to store and to recall.

subject: the stolen key
fact: The stolen key was the original conduit for the summoning spell, but it was replaced by a duplicate cast into the sapphire gem — indicating the killer planned for its loss.
source_quote: The summoning had been worked on a *different* key.

subject: the unresolved connection between gem, key, and victim
fact: Daz sensed a pattern linking the stolen key, the sapphire gem, and the murdered man — a connection a Menzoberranzan child should have recognized — but could not resolve, leaving a critical gap in the investigation.
source_quote: There was a connection sitting in the gem and the stolen key and the murdered man... I reached for it and came up with nothing.

subject: Deadwinter's Eve
fact: Deadwinter's Eve is the date when Daral left the book under the evergreen tree around 11am, prior to his meeting at the keeper's Tower — a pivotal moment in the timeline of the book’s tampering.
source_quote: He'd dropped the book under the evergreen tree, next to the other gifts, around 11am on Deadwinter's Eve...

subject: the identity of the murderer
fact: The central unresolved thread is whether Daral is the killer — a possibility repeatedly pressed by Thorin and Daz, based on his inconsistent timeline and the fact that he never handed the book to anyone.
source_quote: Or, the dude we're talking to is the killer.

subject: the nature of the summoning spell
fact: The summoning spell’s true mechanism — using a duplicate cast into the sapphire gem while the original key was stolen — reveals a sophisticated, premeditated method of concealment, suggesting the killer had arcane knowledge and foresight.
source_quote: Tidy. I'd have done the same.

subject: Fembris's departure
fact: Fembris’s decision to leave his post granted the investigators an hour of unsupervised access to the library — a critical window that may have enabled further evidence gathering or tampering.
source_quote: I did the only sensible thing, which was to note that his departure handed us an hour without supervision and to say nothing of the kind out loud.

subject: the missing original key's location
fact: The original key used in the summoning spell has not been recovered — its whereabouts remain unknown, and its theft is the key to understanding the killer’s method and motive.
source_quote: The summoning had been worked on a *different* key.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is trying to clear his name after being accused of murder; he believes he is being framed and fears for his life, repeatedly stating that if he survives the night, he will ensure everyone wraps their gifts properly with biting wards.
source_quote: if he made it through the night, hint, hint, he'd see to it everyone wrapped their gifts right. Wards on every wrapping, the kind that bite the careless, for everyone.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a drow who has forgotten what matters and remembers what doesn't; he is unable to interpret the sapphire or key despite his expertise in magical artifacts, and he insists the poison only activates upon contact with living tissue.
source_quote: What I can read off it at a glance is next to nothing... staring harder got me less... Why did it turn dark, but it's not dark on the book? Because it goes black after you die.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the stealthiest member of the group; he is skeptical of finding the key due to its ease of concealment but believes the sapphire might still be in someone's possession because it appears innocuous, and he is focused on identifying the killer, not the thief.
source_quote: Zalthir didn't think we'd find the key — too easy to hide. The sapphire, though, somebody might still be holding because it looked like nothing.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool claims to have learned silence and is attempting to grow a nose to smell the poison, showing unusual interest in sensory detection despite his ambiguous nature.
source_quote: Glabbagool announced it had learned silence, then asked whether that was good silence or too loud silence, and tried to grow a nose to smell the poison.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is capable of communicating with beasts; he believes a squirrel in the apothecary may have witnessed something relevant to the investigation.
source_quote: Daz to the apothecary — turned out he could talk to the beasts, and there was a squirrel down there might've seen something.

subject: Candlekeep Faculty
fact: The faculty of Candlekeep are all present at the conference; they are deeply entrenched in academic rivalries, where conflicts are vicious because the stakes are perceived as low, and they are the only potential sources of help in the investigation.
source_quote: everybody hated everybody, it's academia. You know what they say. Fights are so vicious because the stakes are so low.

subject: poison activation
fact: The poison only activates upon contact with a living being's saliva; it remains clear and inert when stored, turning black only after death, which means a search for black residue would fail to locate it.
source_quote: The poison sitting in somebody's room right now wouldn't be black at all. It'd be clear... When I mixed with his saliva, it turned black, okay?

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is an ancient, book-filled archive where the air smells of paper, lamp oil, and old stone; it is currently filled with the faculty of the most learned people on the surface, all gathered for the conference, making it both the scene of the crime and the only source of potential witnesses.
source_quote: The air in Candlekeep still smelled wrong to me. Not bad — paper, lamp oil, old stone warmed by sun I had not seen in months — just wrong...

subject: sapphire
fact: The sapphire is a small, unassuming gemstone taken from the safe; it is believed to be a key component in retrieving the hidden key, and its innocuous appearance makes it a likely object for someone to retain without suspicion.
source_quote: from the safe, a sapphire was taken... the sapphire is actually used to sort of be able to retrieve the key. Crush the stone, the key comes home.

subject: key
fact: The key is a hidden artifact, possibly stored within a locket taken from the victim’s neck; it is believed to unlock something critical, but it is easily concealed and unlikely to be found through a room search.
source_quote: Some locket from around the dude's neck was taken. We assume that inside that locket was the key.

subject: poison vial
fact: The poison is stored in a clear, unmarked vial; it remains inert and invisible until activated by contact with a living being’s saliva, making it nearly impossible to detect unless one knows to look for clear liquid rather than discoloration.
source_quote: A vial of some sort of clear... The poison sitting in somebody's room right now wouldn't be black at all. It'd be clear.

subject: identity of the killer
fact: The true killer has not been identified; the group is aware that the thief of the key and the killer may be two different people, and the investigation must prioritize finding the murderer over recovering the stolen artifacts.
source_quote: And our priority is to find the killer, not who stole the key. Nobody asked us to find the person who stole the key.

subject: squirrel witness
fact: A squirrel in the apothecary may have witnessed the theft or poisoning; its potential testimony is unverified but considered a plausible lead due to Daz’s ability to communicate with beasts.
source_quote: there was a squirrel down there might've seen something, which is a sentence I never thought I'd take seriously.

subject: elapsed time
fact: The investigation is occurring within a narrow window — a single hour — during which the group must divide labor and act before the opportunity passes.
source_quote: Alright, so it looks like we get a freebie hour... I wasn't spending the hour chasing keys.

subject: poison
fact: The poison is a magical hazard that lies dormant until activated by contact with a living being's saliva, then rapidly turns black and causes death; it is not a creature but a lethal substance with behavior resembling a trap or curse.
source_quote: The stuff only wakes up when a living thing touches it... it turned black... because it goes black after you die.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the group's organizer; he prefers clear divisions of labor, insists the priority is finding the killer over recovering stolen items, and coordinates the team’s search efforts, particularly assigning himself to accompany Daral back to the kitchen.
source_quote: I like it that way... And me with Daral, back to the kitchen.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is observing and analyzing the double-strike murder of Janussi and the framing of Daral, identifying A'lai Aivenmore as the prime suspect motivated by ideology and ambition to seize the keep.
source_quote: A drama queen. He knew it; he said it about himself, which is its own kind of telling. I filed the name. A'lai. Ideology and ambition both — a man who kills for the chair and the idea at once.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is the intended target of a framing scheme, suspected of being manipulated into a position where his love of poetry and fiction is seen as a threat by A'lai Aivenmore.
source_quote: Daral arrived at the name like a man arriving at the last line of a poem he'd written. A'lai Aivenmore. The one who wanted the keep. The one about to be dismissed. The one who saw Daral's love of poetry, his love of fiction, as a threat to his approach to the universe.

subject: A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A'lai Aivenmore is the suspected mastermind behind the murder of Janussi and the framing of Daral, seeking to eliminate rivals and ascend to power by exploiting symbolic and psychological tactics.
source_quote: Clear the deck of Janussi. Clear the wood of me. No one left on the council able to prevent his ascension.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was poisoned by a book given to him by Daral, making him the first casualty in a two-part scheme designed to discredit and remove Daral from the council.
source_quote: Janussi was dead. Poisoned by a book Daral had given him.

subject: The Council
fact: The Council is a governing body in which Daral and Janussi held influence, and whose balance is now threatened by A'lai Aivenmore’s calculated elimination of key members.
source_quote: No one left on the council able to prevent his ascension.

subject: double-strike murder
fact: A single act of poison was used to kill Janussi and frame Daral, indicating a premeditated strategy to remove two political obstacles with one move.
source_quote: A killer who buys two outcomes with one cup of poison is a killer who has already drawn the board and decided where every piece lands.

subject: Southern Dining Hall
fact: The Southern Dining Hall contains a lead-lined brass chalice statue of Milil, which Daral recalls was used during the Midsummer Wine ceremony and may have concealed magical interference.
source_quote: We used it for the Midsummer Wine!... The Milil chalice is lead-lined.

subject: Milil's lead-lined chalice
fact: The brass chalice held by the statue of Milil is lead-lined, potentially capable of blocking scrying magic and concealing hidden substances or enchantments.
source_quote: Lead-lined. That's not nothing. Wouldn't lead choke off the magic that hunts down a hidden thing, the same way it blinds a scrying?

subject: the poisoned book
fact: The book given to Janussi by Daral was the vehicle of the poison, chosen for its symbolic and psychological impact to implicate Daral in the murder.
source_quote: Poisoned by a book Daral had given him.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an intelligent ooze with a persistent, hopeful nature, constantly attempting to assist others despite repeated failure, and recently offered to grow a nose to detect poison.
source_quote: *I have learned silence,* he said. ... The eye rose again, eager. He'd try. He always tries.

subject: hidden magic in the chalice
fact: The lead-lined chalice of Milil may have been used to conceal a magical substance or enchantment during the Midsummer Wine ceremony, and its purpose remains unverified.
source_quote: Perhaps somebody hid something in it.

subject: Glabbagool's sensory evolution
fact: Glabbagool is attempting to develop new physical capabilities — including a nose — to enhance his utility, raising the question of whether sentient oozes can biologically adapt beyond their original form.
source_quote: I doubt this is gonna work," I said, "but can Glabbagool try to grow a nose and get a good smell of the poison?

subject: forty minutes of theater
fact: Forty minutes of deliberation and roleplay preceded the decision to investigate the apothecary, indicating the pacing of the group’s investigative process.
source_quote: Then the decision came, because forty minutes of theater is forty minutes, and you have to move.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is methodically analyzing the lead-lined chalice in the dining hall, recognizing its potential to obstruct magical detection and suspecting it may hold hidden evidence.
source_quote: I clocked it and kept it.

subject: Apothecary
fact: The apothecary is the next destination for investigation, where the nature of the poison used in Janussi’s murder may be identified.
source_quote: It seems like at least one of us should check out the apothecary," I said. "Learn more about the poison.

subject: The Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow is a known philosophical or ideological group, referenced for the saying that the most dangerous person is the one who has already decided they've won.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying — or maybe it was Brother Tervin... that the most dangerous person in a room isn't the one with the blade drawn. It's the one who has already decided they've won.

subject: Irony
fact: Irony is a junior avowed who compulsively tells the truth and served food at the Deadwinter supper; she confirms the meal began at 5PM, involved shared platters, and notes Alkrist was unusually cheerful while pitching a book project.
source_quote: At least I can tell you what happened at dinner.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a scholar who was present at the Deadwinter supper; he muttered under his breath, 'Oh, you've been right behind one of us all night,' implying suspicion of insider knowledge or surveillance.
source_quote: Oh, you've been right behind one of us all night.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is a cheerful attendee at the Deadwinter supper who promoted the book project 'Tales of War by the Generals That Waged Them,' which drew criticism from Teles and praise from Janussi.
source_quote: the kind of knowledge that could benefit civilization.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi praised Alkrist’s book project, excused himself after receiving his Secret Santa gift, and dropped the wrapping paper in a wicker basket by the door — later found to be the victim whose heart was stolen.
source_quote: the kind of knowledge that could benefit civilization.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas stormed out of the Deadwinter supper before the gift-giving, creating a break in the timeline that may have allowed access to the chalice or the body.
source_quote: Sylvira Savikas stormed out.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani handed out Secret Santa gifts to the great readers after Sylvira left, matching each gift to its recipient — including Janussi’s unwrapped gift, which he accepted before leaving.
source_quote: Kazryn Nyantani took it on herself to hand out the gifts under the evergreen tree.

subject: Teles
fact: Teles dismissed Alkrist’s book project as implausible, comparing it to a Fheminor Scrivenbark program — suggesting a personal or ideological bias against the project or its proponent.
source_quote: scoffed the project sounded as likely to succeed as some Fheminor Scrivenbark program.

subject: Orrin
fact: Orrin is a junior avowed who served food at the Deadwinter supper alongside Irony and Sprig; all meals were shared from communal platters, with no individual plates.
source_quote: Served by three of them: her, Orrin, and Sprig.

subject: Sprig
fact: Sprig is a junior avowed who served food at the Deadwinter supper; Irony clarified that Sprig doesn’t always lie, countering a joke about his honesty.
source_quote: Sprig doesn't always lie.

subject: Candlekeep Avowed
fact: The junior avowed are Candlekeep’s trainee scholars who served the Deadwinter supper; they operated under strict protocols of shared service and observed the tensions among the great readers, making them potential witnesses or suspects.
source_quote: Three junior avowed lined up near the serving doors.

subject: Deadwinter supper
fact: The Deadwinter supper began at 5PM, featured twelve shared dishes, and included a Secret Santa gift exchange; Janussi left early after receiving his gift, and Sylvira exited before the exchange.
source_quote: The Deadwinter supper began at the 5PM bell.

subject: Secret Santa gift exchange
fact: Kazryn Nyantani distributed wrapped gifts to the great readers after Sylvira left; Janussi received his unwrapped, thanked his donor, and dropped the wrapping paper in a wicker basket before exiting.
source_quote: Janussi took his unwrapped, thanked his secret donor, and excused himself, dropping the wrapping paper in a wicker basket by the door.

subject: inside job
fact: The theft of Janussi’s heart and the use of the lead-lined chalice indicate an inside job — someone with intimate knowledge of Candlekeep’s magic defenses and the chalice’s properties.
source_quote: That's not some random person off the road.

subject: chalice access window
fact: The lead-lined chalice was likely handled after the meal by someone with no legitimate reason to do so — creating a critical window for the theft and a potential witness.
source_quote: Somebody handled it later in the evening.

subject: alibi gap
fact: Sylvira Savikas’s abrupt exit and Janussi’s early departure created a gap in the timeline where access to the chalice and the body could have occurred without observation.
source_quote: Sylvira Savikas stormed out... Janussi... excused himself.

subject: Southern Dining Hall
fact: The Southern Dining Hall is where the Deadwinter supper was held, the chalice was stored, and Janussi’s heart was later found; the alcove and wicker basket near the door are key evidence locations.
source_quote: He started toward the alcove... dropping the wrapping paper in a wicker basket by the door.

subject: lead-lined chalice
fact: The lead-lined chalice was used to conceal Janussi’s heart from far-seeing magic; it was handled during and after the meal, making it the central object in the murder plot.
source_quote: the chalice was lead-lined... would hide a body part from every far-seeing working.

subject: heart and meat cleaver
fact: Janussi’s heart and a blood-stained meat cleaver were found inside the chalice — a deliberate, ritualistic display meant to prevent resurrection and intimidate observers.
source_quote: A heart. And a blood-stained meat cleaver.

subject: Deadwinter night
fact: The murder occurred on the night of the Deadwinter supper, a formal Candlekeep event held annually — a time of ritual, gift-giving, and heightened social tension.
source_quote: The Deadwinter supper began at the 5PM bell.

subject: resurrection-blocking ritual
fact: The removal of Janussi’s heart and placement of the cleaver in the chalice constitutes a resurrection-blocking ritual — a method to prevent magical revival and silence him permanently.
source_quote: They didn't want anybody to be able to bring him back and ask him what happened.

subject: Sprig
fact: Sprig volunteered to taste all twelve dishes served at the meal, insisting despite the chefs saying it was unnecessary; she is the designated poison taster and was present during the poisoning event; she helped Sylvira Savikas find honey after encountering her hoarse and silent at 1:00 a.m.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was the intended target of the poisoning; her death was meant to appear natural, with no connection drawn to the poison taster; she was not the poison taster but was poisoned during the same meal.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas, a tiefling, was encountered at 1:00 a.m. searching by candlelight; she was hoarse and unable to speak, pointing to her throat; she was helped by Sprig with honey; her tiefling nature makes the use of a candlelight unnecessary, raising suspicion that she was not who she appeared to be.

subject: Irony
fact: Irony directed inquiries toward Sprig as the poison taster; she cannot lie but steered conversations without speaking falsely; she has been the target of romantic advances from Teles Ahvoste and may have been trying to avoid them; she dismissed concerns about junior avowed as overinterest.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste, one of the great readers, made persistent romantic advances toward Irony; his behavior may have motivated a scheme to remove Irony from the scene by poisoning Janussi, indirectly threatening Sprig.

subject: Orrin Glass
fact: Orrin Glass, the third waiter, is deaf in one ear and observant; he is the best source for information about interactions between Irony and Teles Ahvoste; he noticed details others missed despite his hearing impairment.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral confirmed the existence of a poison taster role and praised Sprig’s initiative; he is fearful and submissive, especially around Dawnbringer, and does not appear to be the killer.

subject: Candlekeep chefs
fact: The Candlekeep chefs prepared twelve dishes for the meal and advised Sprig that tasting them for poison was unnecessary; they permitted her to volunteer for the role, indicating a culture of deference to initiative.

subject: meal poisoning
fact: A poison was administered during a meal served to the gathering; Janussi was the intended victim; Sprig, the poison taster, survived; the method suggests the poison was delivered via a shared item — the book — rather than food, to avoid killing the taster.

subject: book tampering
fact: The murder weapon was a book that was likely unwrapped and rewrapped; someone observed tampering with the pile of gifts under the non-Christmas Christmas tree; the book was chosen to bypass the poison taster and ensure the victim’s death without implicating the food.

subject: the book
fact: The book was the medium of the poison; it was handled before the meal and likely rewrapped to conceal tampering; it was chosen over food to avoid killing the poison taster, indicating the killer knew of Sprig’s role.

subject: honey
fact: A pot of honey was provided to Sylvira Savikas when she was found hoarse at 1:00 a.m.; it served as a cover for her true purpose — possibly setting down or retrieving something — and may have been used to explain her presence and condition to observers.

subject: non-Christmas Christmas tree
fact: A pile of gifts — mostly books, but also wands and magical artifacts — was stacked under the non-Christmas Christmas tree; this was the location where someone observed tampering with the book that was later used as the poison vector.

subject: kitchens
fact: The kitchens were visited by Sylvira Savikas at 1:00 a.m. under candlelight; Sprig encountered her there and assisted her with honey; the location was used as a cover for an undisclosed activity.

subject: Sylvira's identity
fact: Sylvira Savikas’s behavior — using candlelight despite being a tiefling, being hoarse, and refusing to speak — suggests she may not have been who she appeared to be; this raises the possibility of impersonation or magical disguise.

subject: Irony’s evasion
fact: Irony, who cannot lie, redirected inquiries about the poisoning toward Sprig instead of answering directly; her evasion suggests she knows more than she admits and is protecting someone or something.

subject: killer’s motive
fact: The killer chose to poison via the book rather than the food, indicating knowledge of Sprig’s role as poison taster; this suggests the killer intended to kill Janussi without harming Sprig — implying a personal connection to Sprig or a desire to preserve her.

subject: the honey cover
fact: The honey provided to Sylvira may have been a deliberate distraction to explain her presence in the kitchens at 1:00 a.m. and to mask the act of leaving or retrieving an object — possibly the poison delivery mechanism or a false trail.

subject: 1:00 a.m.
fact: Sylvira Savikas was encountered in the kitchens at 1:00 a.m., and Sprig helped her at that time; this late hour is suspicious and coincides with the timing of the poisoning’s effects.

subject: poison
fact: The poison was slow-acting, designed to kill Janussi at midnight; it was delivered via the book, not food; its formulation suggests the killer knew the victim’s habits and the presence of a poison taster.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is interrogating the wait staff and has identified multiple suspects in the theft of a toxic substance, noting the cut-and-retied string on Janussi's Deadwinter gift as a key clue, and recognizing the coordinated nature of the crime as professionally executed.
source_quote: We're getting more suspects instead of fewer, just to be clear.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was seen holding a scrap of paper toward a candle and dropping it when two junior avowed entered, making him a suspect in the theft of the toxic substance.
source_quote: Alkrist had been holding a small scrap of paper toward a candle, feeding it to the flame, and when two junior avowed walked in, he dropped it.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi's Deadwinter gift had a string that was cut and retied, indicating tampering with the package containing the book inside, and serving as the central clue in the theft investigation.
source_quote: The string tied around Janussi's Deadwinter gift had clearly been cut and retied.

subject: Janussi's Deadwinter gift
fact: The gift contained a book whose wrapping had been opened and the string retied, suggesting the contents were accessed and possibly replaced or altered during the theft.
source_quote: The book sitting wrapped in that package, the string opened and knotted back shut.

subject: peppermint-soaked rag
fact: A peppermint-soaked rag was found beneath the top shelf in the apothecary, alongside a broken vial, indicating a botched attempt to conceal the theft of a dangerous toxin.
source_quote: Under the top shelf I found a peppermint-soaked rag and a broken vial.

subject: broken vial
fact: The broken vial was labeled in Elvish as *Dangerous Toxins*, and contained a substance that, when mixed and built upon, becomes a lethal poison.
source_quote: The shelf above the spillage was labeled, in Elvish, *Dangerous Toxins.* The glass had broken and somebody had tried to hide it.

subject: dragonborn
fact: The dragonborn entered the apothecary alone while the shopkeeper was distracted, broke the vial of dangerous toxin, and stole it, acting as the primary thief in the coordinated crime.
source_quote: A huge lizard skin came in and made a big mess. Something went *bling* and shuddered, and the lizard moved things around, and then left.

subject: Fheminor
fact: Fheminor, a gnome, visited the apothecary at half past two for cold medicine and had left before the theft occurred, ruling her out as the thief but establishing her presence in the timeline.
source_quote: At half past two, the gnome — Fheminor — came for cold medicine. Tincture of horehound, licorice to chew.

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai, a dark-skinned elf, visited the apothecary at three and was led by Leuwin to the greenhouse below, serving as the diversion that kept the shopkeeper away from the upstairs where the theft occurred.
source_quote: At three, A'lai arrived asking for fennel for indigestion, and Leuwin took him down through the rear exit to the greenhouse below.

subject: Leuwin
fact: Leuwin, the elderly satyr apothecary, was distracted by A'lai’s visit and led him to the greenhouse, making him unaware of the theft occurring upstairs, and thus an unwitting participant in the diversion.
source_quote: Leuwin didn't know... because Leuwin wasn't in the room.

subject: Nibbles
fact: Nibbles, the squirrel, witnessed the events through bribes of nuts and confirmed the dragonborn’s presence and actions, serving as the key witness who exposed the coordinated theft.
source_quote: The squirrel popped up... I had nuts. We understood each other immediately.

subject: drow
fact: A drow orchestrated the theft by bribing the squirrel with nuts and arranging the diversion that kept Leuwin occupied, ensuring their hands remained clean of the dangerous toxin.
source_quote: A drow on his knees, bribing a squirrel one nut at a time.

subject: theft of dangerous toxin
fact: The theft of the dangerous toxin was executed through a coordinated two-part operation: a diversion in the greenhouse to distract the apothecary, and a silent theft upstairs by the dragonborn, who broke the vial and removed the substance.
source_quote: A diversion in one room, the theft in another, and the only one of them within reach of the poison is the one who isn't a drow.

subject: origin of the drow's involvement
fact: The drow’s identity and motive remain unknown, as the squirrel could not identify any distinguishing marks, leaving the mastermind of the operation still concealed.
source_quote: I asked whether either of them had any identifying marks. The squirrel didn't know.

subject: Daz — The Squirrel's Testimony at the Oak Tree Apothecary
fact: The Oak Tree Apothecary is a living evergreen oak with a hollowed trunk housing a pharmacy, located on the west grounds of the library, where the theft of the dangerous toxin occurred.
source_quote: The apothecary was a tree. Not a building shaped like a tree, an actual evergreen oak grown out of the burrows in the west of the library grounds...

subject: time of theft
fact: The theft occurred at a quarter past three, after Fheminor had left and while Leuwin was in the greenhouse with A'lai, leaving the upstairs unattended.
source_quote: At a quarter past three, the trouble.

subject: squirrel's testimony
fact: The squirrel's testimony, obtained through nut bribes, reorganized the timeline and identified the dragonborn as the thief and the drow as the orchestrator, exposing the precision of the crime.
source_quote: Because you gave me so many tokens, I saw the person, but Leuwin didn't, because Leuwin wasn't in the room.

subject: Orrin
fact: Orrin provided the critical clue about the cut-and-retied string on Janussi's Deadwinter gift, which Thorin recognized as the key indicator of internal tampering.
source_quote: And then Orrin handed me the one that mattered. Something out of the ordinary: the string tied around Janussi's Deadwinter gift had clearly been cut and retied.

subject: cut-and-retied string
fact: The cut-and-retied string on Janussi's Deadwinter gift was the physical signature of the theft, proving the package had been opened and resealed by someone inside the room with access to the gifts.
source_quote: The cut string was the rock in the right place. Nobody came in from outside. This was somebody who'd been at the table.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is searching the Readers' Chambers, having received eight names, and is now focused on interpreting clues left behind by the occupants, including A'lai Aivenmore, Alkrist, Bookwyrm, and others.
source_quote: The list came to me as eight names... I asked the only question that mattered.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas was the first name pointed at by everyone, and Zalthir decided to skip her chambers for now, recognizing her as an obvious but potentially misleading target.
source_quote: Sylvira Savikas, whom everyone had already pointed at... I'm gonna skip Sylvira for now.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is suspected of having poisoned himself, and Zalthir chose to skip his chambers, understanding that leaving him uninvestigated makes him the obvious suspect — a tactic Thorin would endorse.
source_quote: But Daral's the one who's poisoned himself, right?... Skip him and he becomes the obvious suspect, of course — Thorin would say it dry, and he would be right.

subject: A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A'lai Aivenmore’s chambers were sparse and tasteful, containing fine glassware, good ceramics, a large mirror, and a portrait of himself — indicating a man who liked to be looked at, including by himself.
source_quote: A'lai's chambers first. Sparse, tasteful — fine glassware, good ceramics, a large mirror, and a portrait of himself on the wall.

subject: dove cage
fact: A dove cage in A'lai's chambers was built for five birds, but only two were present — suggesting three messages had been sent recently, and the absence of the other birds is a significant clue.
source_quote: The cage was built for five. Two birds sat in it... There had been more than two. Three messages had gone somewhere, and recently.

subject: glass jars of poisoned rats
fact: Alkrist’s chambers contained sealed glass jars holding dead rats with blistered, pustule-ridden skin — indicating active study of poison and its effects on the body.
source_quote: Sealed glass jars holding dead rats, their skin blistered and risen into pustules. I have seen what poison does to a body.

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: A black leather-bound copy of 1001 Tashalian Nights lay open to the tale of a military commander poisoned by a magic horn coated in Midnight Tears, with a bookmark left precisely on that page.
source_quote: A book — black leather, stars and gold filigree... The bookmark sat on the tale of a military commander, poisoned by a gift of surrender — a magic horn whose mouthpiece had been coated in Midnight Tears.

subject: Midnight Tears
fact: Midnight Tears is a poison referenced in a marked story and associated with a poisoned gift — now a key thread linking Alkrist’s study of poison to a potential assassination method.
source_quote: Midnight Tears. I kept the name where I would not lose it.

subject: Alkrist’s chambers
fact: Alkrist’s chambers were lavishly furnished, containing expensive cloth, fashionable art, a spellbook, jars of poisoned rats, and a marked copy of 1001 Tashalian Nights — indicating a man of wealth, intellect, and obsession with poison.
source_quote: Alkrist next, and Alkrist did not believe in restraint. Lavish furniture, expensive cloth, fashionable art hung to be noticed. His spellbook on the desk... And on the desk beside it, sealed glass jars...

subject: Bookwyrm’s chambers
fact: Bookwyrm’s chambers occupied half the top floor, were clean and neatly arranged, contained no obvious clues, and were free of poison — a deliberate absence that itself became information.
source_quote: Bookwyrm last... I found nothing. Glabbagool tasted the air and found no poison in it. A clean room. That, too, was information.

subject: Readers' Tower
fact: The Readers' Tower is a multi-room structure with locked doors and staircases of increasing difficulty, where each chamber holds hidden clues, and access is physically and mentally taxing for the investigator.
source_quote: A staircase of locked doors, each step taller than the last... I went down the list in order, with two corrections.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient, shapeless ooze that flows through spaces inaccessible to humans, absorbs knowledge from environments, and assists Zalthir by reading what he cannot understand — now an integral partner in the investigation.
source_quote: I had Glabbagool. The ooze had come out of the bag eager... He flowed where I could not reach; I read what he could not understand.

subject: locked safe
fact: A locked safe in Alkrist’s chambers had an opening no wider than a finger’s width — too narrow for Glabbagool to penetrate — and remains unopened, preserving its secret.
source_quote: Beside it, a locked safe... The opening was a finger's width, no more — a true safe... Glabbagool could not thin himself past it.

subject: reading the bookmarked tale
fact: Zalthir read the bookmarked tale in 1001 Tashalian Nights about a commander poisoned by a magic horn coated in Midnight Tears, and connected it to the jars of poisoned rats in Alkrist’s chambers.
source_quote: A man with jars of poisoned rats had marked his page on a story about a poisoned gift... I set the book back exactly as it lay.

subject: missing three doves
fact: The absence of three doves from the five-bird cage suggests three messages were dispatched — a key thread linking A'lai’s chambers to a covert communication network.
source_quote: Three messages had gone somewhere, and recently. I kept that.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced as a tactician who understands psychological manipulation in investigations — specifically that leaving a suspect uninvestigated makes him the obvious suspect.
source_quote: Thorin would put it plainly: we aren't hunting Daral, we're keeping him on a hook... Thorin would say it dry, and he would be right.

subject: Brother Heslin
fact: Brother Heslin is remembered as a possible instructor in the art of reading meaning from objects — a skill Zalthir now applies in his investigation, though he did not learn it at the time.
source_quote: There was a class for this, somewhere in the monastery — reading what an object meant rather than what it was. Brother Heslin, maybe, or the tall one who smelled of incense.

subject: investigation of the Readers' Chambers
fact: Zalthir conducted a methodical investigation of eight chambers in the Readers' Tower, uncovering three converging clues: missing doves, poisoned rats, and a bookmarked tale of Midnight Tears — forming the core of the current lead.
source_quote: We had several. A cage missing three birds. Jars of blistered rats. A page marked to a poisoning by gift.

subject: one night
fact: The entire investigation of the Readers' Chambers occurred over the span of one night, a compressed timeframe that heightens the urgency and intensity of Zalthir’s deductions.
source_quote: Eight rooms. One night. I asked the only question that mattered.
